pr_title: Do not read position when tar archive stream is unseekable
pr_body:
Fixes: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/70172

The position was being read at the very last moment of creating the archive, to set the archive size one byte after the empty records. This causes an exception to be thrown when compressing directly into a gzip stream, which is unseekable (position cannot be accessed).

cc @rainersigwald

issue_context.title: Creating a tar directly into a GZipStream crashes when writing final records
issue_context.body:
The root cause is that we access the position, which is unsupported by GZipStream (unseekable stream).

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blame/218a4b1dad3f73eec8f9898761501c4cfa14698e/src/libraries/System.Formats.Tar/src/System/Formats/Tar/TarWriter.cs#L314

The fix would be to detect if the stream is seekable. If it is, then we can set the length to the position. Otherwise, we skip that step.

Thanks @rainersigwald for [reporting this](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/65951#issuecomment-1145209082).

review_comments:
We have a test that verifies the behavior of the `TarEntry.DataStream` when reading an unseekable stream:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2389815a1bc810b5b3c39586b570cbaae2f0f3a5/src/libraries/System.Formats.Tar/tests/TarReader/TarReader.GetNextEntry.Tests.cs#L165

But that test wasn't creating an archive using `TarWriter` against an unseekable stream, hence why this bug wasn't caught before. That's why I'm also adding this extra test to write to a generic unseekable stream.
are these tests related to the fix?

Yes. This test passes a `GZipStream` (an unseekable stream) to the `TarWriter`. `TarWriter` will finish adding the entries, then will add the two empty records, and then it would've called that incorrect `SetLength` call (which I just removed completely since it's not needed).
